title: Instruments at the Deep Ellum jam sessions and the washtub bass
summary: The players were mostly guitars and piano, with a two-string washtub bass and harmonica. The scene was friendly, with no black-white feeling, and it ended around 1928.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Picking up a first guitar or banjo, self-taught

blocks.x: The main instruments were piano and guitar.
Guitar, yes. And sometimes that lap string bass on a washtub. Sometimes two strings they would play sometimes.
What did they call that instrument?
I don't know. But Crawford, what?
They call it here, they call it a tub of form.
I never did hear, I don't know what the, uh, washtub bass is what I think I used to hear, but I'm not sure.
And they'd have two strings sometimes.
Two strings? How would they be attached?
I don't know, but they would have two strings there. He'd play first one, then the other, leaning it over to get, uh, tension, to get, uh, the right notes and all.
Mm-hmm. Gee. This was the first time you had heard a bass used in this kind of music.
Yes. I hadn't heard anything used in this kind of music before. It got a big kick out of going up there with him.
And would all these, would this be an ensemble group of guitars and piano and bass and French art?

Just anybody who would come in would sit down there and play, and we'd play a while, and they'd all laugh and talk around, and they'd make fun. But, uh, very, it was, uh, not satire. They would just make, uh, pleasant fun, you know, of all the pianists, but they'd still show me all their stuff because I was just a kid, and of course they saw that I liked them, and there was never any feeling of black and white at all, never involved, which was kind of strange. And sometimes I'd stay behind the bar in the back room or somewhere and go to sleep, while Daddy would go off doing some kind of business or work or something. And at one time, when there was some kind of a fight, some of the people would hustle me out of there, and they sort of took care of me. It wasn't between five and, uh, it stopped about 1928, I guess. Uh, five, between five and ten, five, six, seven, eight, nine.
